chapter: Louis Armstrong, Basie and New York studio scene
title: Louis Armstrong as the trinity of his life; peeking in at the Grand Terrace as a paper boy
summary: Hinton, delivering papers at dawn, watched the Grand Terrace staff clean up and passed rehearsals at the old Peerless Theatre.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: You do have…you have had over the years a wonderful relationship with other, you talked about Cab Calloway and you had a wonderful relationship with Louis Armstrong. Tell me about that.

Well Louie was the trinity of my life. When I was 15 and delivering newspapers at 5:30 in the morning, I would go by there, peeping in the window with my paper sack on my back, seeing the waiters putting the chairs up on the tables and the black musicians with the tuxedo on and a nice cold glass in his hand. And the lady waiting for him you know. I would say hey this is it. And then I would go by [unintelligible] rehearsal and it was on my paper route right there on the boulevard, there was the Grand Terrace and I would go by the rehearsal…
It was South Parkway and Oakwood Boulevard. It‟s 39th Street, right there.
